goal: Adds a safety check so the wallet rejects a signed PSBT if the external signer silently changed an output or used an output-non-committing sighash.
Protects users of hardware/external signers from a compromised or buggy signer altering where funds go.
reviewability: Paused: a maintainer says this work has already been folded into a different PR (#36114) that revamps the mock signer.
Reviewing the current diff is likely wasted effort since the approach is being superseded.

A technical question about allowing ANYONECANPAY sighash was raised and answered without pushback (junbyjun1238, achow101).
No blocking objections, but the PR was absorbed into #36114 rather than merged on its own (Sjors).

result.summary: This PR adds a post-signing validation step in ExternalSigner::SignTransaction that compares the PSBT returned by an external signer against the original PSBT sent to it, rejecting the reply if outputs (amount, script, count) were altered or if an unsafe sighash type (one that does not commit to all outputs) was used. It ships mock-signer test infrastructure to simulate a rogue signer and functional tests exercising each corruption case. The author notes the added tests were 'partially vibe-coded.'
result.problem: A compromised or buggy external signer could return a PSBT with silently altered outputs or a sighash type that does not commit to all outputs, potentially sending funds to the wrong destination without the wallet noticing. Users relying on hardware/external signers currently have no automated defense against this and would need to manually verify the signed PSBT, which is not convenient via RPC.

resolved_concerns: junbyjun1238 asked whether allowing SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY as 'safe' is correct since it lets other inputs be added; achow101 explained this is fine because the wallet's own inputs and outputs remain committed, resolving the question without pushback.

result.card: This PR adds a check in ExternalSigner::SignTransaction that rejects a signed PSBT if the external signer altered any output or used a sighash type that doesn't commit to all outputs, guarding against a compromised or buggy hardware/external signer silently redirecting funds. It ships mock-signer infrastructure and functional tests simulating several rogue-signer scenarios, though the author calls the tests 'partially vibe-coded.' Maintainer achow101 gave a lukewarm 'Concept OK I guess,' noting external signers are already assumed trusted so such checks have limited marginal value, and resolved a question about whether allowing ANYONECANPAY sighash is safe. As of 2026-08-28, reviewer Sjors says the work was absorbed into a different open PR (#36114) that revamps the signer mock, making this PR's current form likely superseded and low priority to review as-is. No dependency blocks it formally, but #36114 has effectively taken over its scope.
